primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Type I collagen is a heterotrimer of two alpha-1(I) and one alpha-2(I) chains with a Gly-X-Y repeating triple-helical region. Pathogenic variants can reduce type I collagen quantity or disrupt helix structure, producing bone fragility and characteristic extraskeletal connective-tissue manifestations.
vignette: A child has multiple fractures after minimal trauma, blue-gray sclerae, and a family history of similar bone fragility. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in COL1A1.
lead: Which normal protein is directly affected by this mutation?
correct: Type I collagen, composed of two alpha-1 chains and one alpha-2 chain
distractors: Type II collagen, a major collagen of hyaline cartilage
Type III collagen, abundant in blood vessels and hollow organs
Type IV collagen, a network-forming basement-membrane collagen
Fibrillin-1, a component of extracellular microfibrils
distractor_notes: Type II collagen is abundant in cartilage and is encoded by COL2A1, not COL1A1.
Type III collagen is encoded by COL3A1 and is prominently affected in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
Type IV collagen forms basement-membrane networks and is distinct from fibrillar type I collagen.
Fibrillin-1 is affected in Marfan syndrome and is not a collagen chain.
key_expl: COL1A1 and COL1A2 encode the alpha chains of type I collagen, the principal fibrillar collagen of bone, dermis, tendon, and other connective tissues. The mature type I collagen molecule contains two alpha-1(I) chains and one alpha-2(I) chain arranged as a triple helix. Abnormal quantity or structure produces osteogenesis imperfecta.
objective: Identify type I collagen as the COL1A1/COL1A2 product responsible for classic osteogenesis imperfecta.
